question.value: What do very high resolution ALMA long-baseline continuum, CO and H2O observations reveal about the lensed submillimeter galaxy SDP.81 at z=3.042, including emission at the lens centre?

evidence.quote: We present initial results of very high resolution Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the $z$=3.042 gravitationally lensed submillimeter galaxy HATLAS J090311.6+003906 (SDP.81).

bands.value: Band 4 (~2 mm), Band 6 (~1.3 mm), Band 7 (~1.0 mm)

evidence.quote: Observations were carried out in Band 4 ($\sim$2 mm), Band 6 ($\sim$1.3 mm) and Band 7 ($\sim$1.0 mm).

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Per band 7.5 GHz split into 4 spws: three 15.6 MHz continuum spws and one line spw

evidence.quote: the total available 7.5 GHz bandwidth was divided into four spectral windows (spws): three 15.6 MHz channel width spws
centered on the redshifted CO $J$=5-4 line ($v_{\rm rest}$ = 576.267 GHz)
the CO $J$=8-7 line ($v_{\rm rest}$ = 921.799 GHz)
covered the redshifted CO $J$=10-9 line ($v_{\rm rest}$ = 1151.985 GHz)
Continuum images were integrated over a bandwidth of $\sim$7 GHz
baseline lengths ranged from $\sim$15 m to 15 km.
The resulting synthesized beam sizes range from $\sim$23–60 mas.
The total on-source integration times were 5.9, 4.4 and 5.6 hours in Bands 4, 6, and 7, respectively.
were carried out in 2014 October as part of the 2014 ALMA Long Baseline Campaign

findings_qualitative.value: CO emission traces the arcs but morphologies differ between CO transitions and from continuum

claims.hypothesis: Can ALMA long baselines resolve the lensed SMG consistently with previous fluxes?
claims.experiment: Continuum imaging at 151, 236, 290 GHz with baselines to 15 km
claims.result: Beams as fine as 23 mas; fluxes consistent with PdBI/SMA
claims.finding: Fluxes remain consistent despite large resolution increase

evidence.quote: The ALMA continuum and spectral line fluxes are consistent with previous Plateau de Bure Interferometer and Submillimeter Array observations

claims.hypothesis: Is the central lens continuum emission from an AGN in the lens?
claims.experiment: Flux at lens position in three bands plus FIRST 1.4 GHz
claims.finding: Emission consistent with the core of the foreground lensing galaxy

evidence.quote: with a spectral index that is consistent with emission from the core of the foreground lensing galaxy

claims.hypothesis: Can H2O be detected at higher resolution?
claims.experiment: Tapered H2O image from short baselines
claims.result: Emission clearly detected in E arc at ~0.9"
claims.finding: Most resolved thermal H2O detection in an extragalactic source

evidence.quote: provides the most resolved detection to date of thermal H$_{\rm 2}$O emission in an extragalactic source

why_this_method.value: robust=1 weighting critical due to lack of 200-500 m baseline coverage

evidence.quote: the use of robust weighting (*robust*=1) was critical for achieving acceptable image quality

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: nterms=2 combined Band 6&7 imaging rejected as S/N too low; tapered image approach used

evidence.quote: The SNR of the full-resolution $uv$ data was found to be too low for the algorithm to determine the spectral index

limitations_admitted.value: Differential lensing cannot be quantified without detailed lens modelling, which is beyond scope

evidence.quote: Without detailed modeling, any effect from differential magnification cannot be quantified

referee_caveats_inferred: No lens modelling, so arc fluxes are magnified and differential magnification is unaddressed
Central-source AGN interpretation relies on a non-simultaneous FIRST flux
